prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Desktop Pet Controls", "Right-click your pet anytime to open settings, feed them, or temporarily send them to sleep."]
1: ["Choose Your Desktop Companion"]
2: ["Preparing Your Pet Workspace", "Your companion will appear seamlessly over your open desktop windows once generation completes."]
3: ["Select Your Adoption Method"]
4: ["Signing in connects your desktop pet data to your cloud account so your pet is never lost."]
5: ["You can minimize this window. We will send a system notification when your pet is ready!"]
6: ["Meet Your Virtual Desktop Buddy", "A lightweight companion that sits on your taskbar and keeps you company while you work or game."]
7: ["For optimal results, upload a well-lit, front-facing photo without crowded backgrounds."]
8: ["Your Companion Has Arrived!", "Check the corner of your desktop screen to see your new pet floating over your apps."]
9: ["Sign in to save your pet progress. If the login popup does not open, check your system browser settings."]

verdicts.problem: Asks for a personal photo of the user.
